sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Daily snapshot captured 2026-11-16 01:34 UTC; date range 2026-11-16 through 2026-11-16. Ranking follows GitHub Trending daily; star gains are partial-day figures.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-facing software dominates today's list: office and frontend protocols, agent skills, human review loops, and browser tools all rank highly. Univer leads with 2,354 stars today; the common thread is building the connective tissue and oversight around coding agents rather than a new model release.

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: An embeddable office SDK for adding spreadsheet, document, collaboration, and file-processing features to products and agents.
sections.content: An extensible office foundation with APIs and events for applications and agents; the day's strongest star gain.
sections.why_notable: The day's strongest star gain; its README describes an extensible office foundation with APIs and events for applications and agents.

sections.title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
sections.description: An event-based protocol for connecting AI agents to user-facing applications.
sections.content: An open, lightweight event protocol that standardizes agent-to-application interaction, with streaming and human-in-the-loop patterns.
sections.why_notable: A strong protocol-layer signal; its README emphasizes interoperable events, streaming, and human-in-the-loop interfaces.

sections.title: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src
sections.description: Guidance intended to keep coding agents aligned with current web-platform practices.
sections.content: Domain-specific web-platform guidance aims to steer coding agents toward current practices.
sections.why_notable: The second-largest daily gain, pointing to demand for domain-specific knowledge that steers code-generating agents.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: Open-standard agent skills and plugins for Google Stitch design and build workflows.
sections.content: Cross-agent skills and plugins organize Stitch design, build, and utility workflows according to the Agent Skills open standard.
sections.why_notable: Shows demand for reusable, cross-agent skill packages rather than one-off prompts.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says these skills require the Stitch MCP server to be configured and running.

sections.title: backnotprop/plannotator
sections.description: A review surface for annotating agent plans, artifacts, and code changes, then routing feedback back to agents.
sections.content: A local browser-based review flow for plans, specifications, artifacts, diffs, and pull requests across multiple coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Its README documents a local browser-based review flow spanning multiple agents and artifact types, matching the day's human-oversight theme.

sections.title: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
sections.description: Chrome DevTools access for coding agents, available through MCP and a CLI.
sections.content: Gives agents live-browser control and inspection for automation, debugging, and performance analysis.
sections.why_notable: Adds real-browser debugging, automation, and performance analysis to agent workflows; it has the largest existing star base among today's top entries.
sections.unique_caveat: The README notes that MCP clients can inspect browser contents; usage statistics are enabled by default, with an opt-out flag.

sections.title: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
sections.description: Claude Code skills for market analysis, technical charting, screening, and trading workflows.
sections.content: A domain-specific skill pack for investment research and trading workflows, outside the dominant software-engineering use case.
sections.why_notable: A domain-specific skill pack outside the dominant software-engineering use case; GitHub's daily list ranks it among the strongest gainers.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: A code-review tool combining deterministic checks with an LLM agent and line-level comments.
sections.content: Reads diffs and code context to produce structured, line-level review comments using configurable LLMs and deterministic rules.
sections.why_notable: Represents a practical hybrid for AI code review, with the README describing tool-assisted contextual review and a precision-oriented trade-off.

sections.title: Tencent/LoopForge
sections.description: Self-hosted workflows for coding-agent delivery with scripts and human approval gates.
sections.content: Orchestrates supported coding assistants through self-hosted and local workflows with explicit human approvals.
sections.why_notable: A concrete orchestration signal: multiple coding agents are routed through locally controlled, approval-based delivery.

sections.title: NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator
sections.description: A framework for evaluating agent skills with quality gates, overlap detection, and live behavior tests.
sections.content: A measurement layer for the skill ecosystem that evaluates quality, overlap, and effects on agent behavior.
sections.why_notable: Adds a measurement layer to the expanding skill ecosystem, evaluating whether skills change agent behavior rather than only inspecting their text.

sections.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
sections.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team workflows.
sections.content: A security-oriented agent skill bundle; the Trending description cites 82 skills, 15 slash commands, and vulnerability-class coverage.
sections.why_notable: Extends the agent-skills pattern into security work, with the listing describing coverage across vulnerability classes and report patterns.

sections.title: ggml-org/ggml
sections.description: A tensor library for machine learning.
sections.content: A foundational C++ tensor library and a lower-momentum counterpoint to today's agent-application cluster.
sections.why_notable: A lower-momentum counterpoint to the agent-application cluster: foundational ML systems work still appears on today's list.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository description is broad and does not by itself specify an end-user application.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: The dominant cluster is agent-facing software: office and UI interfaces, reusable skills, review/approval loops, and browser/code tooling. TypeScript leads with 6 of 12 repositories; Python has 3, Go 2, and C++ 1. ggml is the lone clearly foundational ML-library counterpoint.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's signal is less about inventing new agents than making them usable in real products: giving them interfaces, skills, browser access, review channels, and controlled delivery pipelines. The unusually strong TypeScript showing fits that application-layer tilt, while the security, evaluation, and code-review repos show an accompanying push toward oversight and reliability.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, read at 2026-11-16 01:34 UTC. GitHub REST repository and commit endpoints corroborated star totals, languages, default branches, latest commits, and repository status for all 12 entries. GitHub Search API query created:2026-11-14..2026-11-16 pushed:>=2026-11-14 stars:>100 was checked for newly created projects; duplicate/noisy results were excluded. Daily gains are partial-day values from the matching Trending page.
